newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF signs deal to consider j-v in China.
newsitem.headline: BASF signs deal to consider j-v in China.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Friday that it had signed a agreement with Chinese partners to consider entering a joint-venture to produce polyurethane materials.
In a statement BASF said that the new plants would cost about 800 million marks and that they should become operational by 2001.
BASF, which has invested heavily in the Chinese market in the last years, signed the agreement with the China Petrochemical Corp, Gao-Qiao Petro-Chemical Corp and Shanghai Hua YI Group Company.
The new plant would produced up to 100,000 tonnes annually of TDI and MDI.
BASF said that if technical and economic studies show the cooperation would be a success, a letter of intent should be signed soon.
